enonce_intro_markdown: Given that the events $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the condition for which $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two events are mutually exclusive when they cannot occur at the same time, i.e. they have no outcome in common:

$A\cap B=\varnothing$, so $P(A\cap B)=0$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, given that $P(A)=\dfrac16$ and $P(B)=\dfrac34$, find $P(A\cup B)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For mutually exclusive events, $P(A\cup B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) = P(A)+P(B)$.

$P(A\cup B)=\dfrac16+\dfrac34=\dfrac{2}{12}+\dfrac{9}{12}=\dfrac{11}{12}$.

**$P(A\cup B)=\dfrac{11}{12}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $P(A^{c})$ (with $P(A)=\dfrac16$ as above). *[5 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$A^{c}$ is the complement of $A$ (the event "$A$ does not occur"), so

$P(A^{c}) = 1 - P(A) = 1-\dfrac16=\dfrac56$.

**$P(A^{c})=\dfrac56$.**
